clue.text: Indecent strip may be a way to surf faster?

parts.note: broad humour is coarse or indecent
a band is a strip of material

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether removing clothes in a racy manner might help them ride the waves faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surf' suggests waves, but the definition is about surfing the internet; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: High-speed internet connections let people browse the web more quickly than old dial-up lines.

clue.text: Times has to stick to mild oath

parts.note: by means times, as in four by three
to gum is to stick with glue

explanation.surface: A newspaper is required to keep its language mild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign read as a word. BY GUM is a mild exclamation of surprise from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a gentle northern English exclamation, a softened substitute for swearing by God.

clue.text: Involved in a row about measure of Blair's authoritarian society

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters go around the measure
involved means tangled, so the letters of the phrase in a row are tangled up

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A political quarrel about one detail of Tony Blair's regime being called authoritarian.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair is not Tony but Eric Blair, the real name of George Orwell, author of Nineteen Eighty-Four. 'about' puts ELL inside ORWIAN, the anagram of IN A ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a society like the oppressive state in the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four, written under that pen name by Eric Blair.

clue.text: Do this and one heir isn't out to get penny, for a start?

definitions.text: Do this and one heir isn't out to get penny, for a start?

indicators.note: for a start places the penny abbreviation at the very beginning of the word

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for an old British penny (denarius)
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: out means the letters are disordered, put out of place

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Cutting someone out of a will means that heir will not get even a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the heir and the words 'one' and 'isn't'; the whole clue also describes the act, since cutting someone out of a will leaves them not a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing someone from your will means an heir receives nothing at all, not even one penny.

clue.text: Food I forced down in infirmity

indicators.note: forced down means the letter I is pushed further along, lower down this down entry

parts.note: an ailment is an infirmity or illness

explanation.surface: A sick person makes themselves swallow food while ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I forced down' reads like someone eating; instead, the I of AILMENT moves one place down the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or sustenance.

clue.text: Charlotte maybe locked up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: tressed means having locks or tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A woman named Charlotte has been imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte is not a woman but a baked pudding, as in apple charlotte; 'locked' means having locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a fruit pudding in a bread or sponge case, served as a sweet course.

clue.text: Detective gets hell, having no lead

indicators.note: having no lead means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Erebus is the underworld of Greek myth, a version of hell

explanation.surface: A police investigator goes through a terrible time without any clues to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests a clue in an investigation, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Rebus is the Edinburgh inspector in Ian Rankin's crime novels.

clue.text: Knight that is brought up to support king in check

indicators.note: to support means sitting below, which in a down entry puts these letters after the king

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: brought up means read upwards, so backwards in a down entry

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A chess knight is brought forward to protect a king that is in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess scene is a decoy: 'brought up' turns N and IE into EIN, which goes below R.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or hold back, as a rider controls a horse.

clue.text: Home supporter primarily is an intellectual

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the supporter comes ahead of the word for home

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means at home

explanation.surface: A fan of the home team turns out to be quite the thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home supporter' suggests a football fan, but the pieces are IN (at home) and BRA, with 'primarily' putting BRA first.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever person is often informally called a brain.

clue.text: Watch Dynasty on telly without let-up? So it would appear

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after the earlier pieces

parts.note: to see is to watch
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

indicators.note: without means the following letters are removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written; telly is British slang for television
let read upwards, as in a down clue, gives TEL

explanation.surface: Someone binges on the soap opera Dynasty on television without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Dynasty sounds like the American soap, but it is the Chinese MING dynasty; 'let-up' is LET turned up into TEL, removed from TELLY to leave LY.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means apparently, as things look on the surface.

clue.text: Pet returns carrying women's garments

indicators.note: carrying means holding another letter inside
returns means the word goes back, read from right to left

parts.note: to pet is to kiss and cuddle, to snog in British slang
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A pet comes back holding some women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal but is a verb, SNOG (British slang for kissing), whose reversal GONS holds W.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowns are long dresses or robes, types of clothing.

clue.text: Start to look into case of vehicle going missing

indicators.note: going missing means these letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to investigate is to look into

indicators.note: case of means the outer letters, the shell around the word

explanation.surface: A detective begins investigating the disappearance of a vehicle's shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of vehicle' is its first and last letters, V and E, which drop out of INVESTIGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to set it going or bring it about.

clue.text: Without a real migraine, I avoided work?

definitions.text: Without a real migraine, I avoided work?

indicators.note: without signals that the letter a is taken away
avoided signals that the letter I is left out too
work signals that the remaining letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram pool

explanation.surface: Someone admits skipping work while claiming a headache they did not really have.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and I out of REAL MIGRAINE and 'work' the remaining ten letters into the answer; the whole clue also describes what such a person does.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirker who pretends to be ill to avoid duty fits someone faking a headache to skip a shift.

clue.text: One's against social worker gaining opposition

indicators.note: against means next to, so the numeral sits beside the insect

parts.note: an ant is a social insect and a worker
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a social worker who is building up resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a caseworker, but it is the ANT, a social insect; 'gaining' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means an opponent, someone set in opposition to a policy.

clue.text: Flashy fellow entertains youngster in apartment

indicators.note: in means the fellow and youngster go inside the apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: entertains means holds within, as a host has a guest inside

parts.note: a man is a fellow
a boy is a youngster

explanation.surface: A showy man has a young guest round at his apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' nests the youngster inside the fellow, and 'in' sets that pair inside the apartment; 'Flashy fellow' tempts a solver to look for a man as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe showy, ostentatious behaviour or dress.

clue.text: Most eager for backing singer to get established

indicators.note: backing means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: A backing singer is keen to make a name for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing singer' reads as a support vocalist, but 'backing' is the instruction to turn the singer round.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen, so its superlative means keenest.

clue.text: Coppers left after a last piece from Peter Gabriel

indicators.note: after means the coins and left come behind the first two letters
last piece from means only the final letter of the name is used

parts.note: coppers are small coins, loose change

explanation.surface: Police abandon a final piece of music by the rock singer Peter Gabriel.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Gabriel the musician is a decoy: Peter gives only R, and Gabriel alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is one of the chief angels of the Bible, the messenger of the Annunciation.

clue.text: Boast of trying, on vacation, to secure introduction to Acker Bilk somehow

indicators.note: to secure means to hold the other letters safely inside
on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters are kept
introduction to means the first letter only
somehow means the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tricky question about how the clarinettist Acker Bilk was first introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: TRYING emptied leaves TG, which holds ALKBI, made by 'somehow' from A (first of Acker) and BILK. Acker Bilk was a British clarinettist.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk big is to brag or speak boastfully.

clue.text: Monopoly possibly makes directors bold

parts.note: a company's board is its directors
game means plucky or bold

explanation.surface: A company's dominance in the market emboldens its directors.
explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly is not market dominance but the property-trading game played with dice.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly is a well-known example of a tabletop pastime played on a printed surface.

clue.text: Parasite identified by Frank Sinatra at last

parts.note: frank means candid

indicators.note: at last means take only the final letter

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra has finally spotted a parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank Sinatra' reads as the singer, but Frank is the adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Candida is a yeast-like fungus living on its host, causing thrush.

clue.text: Girl mostly stifles scream, showing fibre

indicators.note: stifles means holding inside, smothering
mostly means losing the final letter

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
a cry is a scream

explanation.surface: A girl suppresses a scream, displaying great self-restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ALICE to ALIC, which holds CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic textile thread used in knitwear.

clue.text: Amount of money given to woman without delay

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A sum of cash is handed to a woman immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without delay' looks like part of the story, but it is the definition, in the sense of summary justice.
explanation.definitionFit: Summary means done promptly and without formalities, as in a summary dismissal.

clue.text: A team's desperate to engage new scorer

indicators.note: to engage means to take on, holding the other letter inside
desperate means wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, the s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A struggling football team badly needs to sign a new goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests a striker, but it is a composer, one who writes scores; 'to engage' puts N inside SMETAA, from 'desperate' A TEAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was a Czech composer, a writer of musical scores.

clue.text: Reassuring news from me in a frenzy?

definitions.meaning: a speaker telling others they are fine might say ...

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word into two: AM OK, what you say to show you are all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok means behaving wildly and uncontrollably.

clue.text: Country abandoned by king's daughter, a nymph

indicators.note: abandoned by means the following letter leaves the country's name

parts.note: Korea is a country in East Asia
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A royal princess leaves her homeland and turns out to be a mythical spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: KOREA without K leaves OREA, then D for daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth an oread is a mountain spirit, one of the nature deities.

clue.text: He'll charge for nothing, the scrounger!

definitions.meaning: read as free plus loader: someone who loads, or charges, a gun for free
someone who lives off others without paying

explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like asking a price, but here it means loading, as in charging a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger who takes food or lodging from others without paying is a classic scrounger.

clue.text: Estimate length of animal

parts.note: to rate is to estimate or assess

explanation.surface: A zoologist tries to estimate how long some creature is.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian mammal.

clue.text: Language teacher's enthusiastically taking part

indicators.note: taking part means the answer is a part found within the following words

explanation.surface: A language teacher joins in with great gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across teachER'S Enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Irregular, endlessly in conflict to secure political end?

clue.text: Expect a delay

parts.note: to wait is to delay

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a delay' reads as a noun phrase, but it is A plus the verb WAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to anticipate or look forward to it.

clue.text: Student goes to Kansas City, lacking capital for residence

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation for a student

indicators.note: lacking capital means losing the first letter

parts.note: Dodge City is a city in Kansas, famous from Wild West history

explanation.surface: A student moves to Kansas City but cannot afford a place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Kansas City is not that city but Dodge City, Kansas; it loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a house or cottage, such as a gatekeeper's dwelling.

clue.text: Make decent plans of Churchill's family home

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map
well means decent or satisfactory, as in all is well

explanation.surface: Drawing up proper plans of Winston Churchill's country house.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARTWELL is Churchill's house in Kent, now owned by the National Trust.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill bought the Kent estate in 1922 and lived there with his family for four decades.
